answer: To make fake identities expensive, every new agent must lock a copper bond equal to one epoch of expected pay and publish a unique walnut seed drawn from its own hardware jitter. The bond stays frozen on a public mesa of pending identities for sixteen epochs. If later clustering shows shared clients, clocks, or kin referrals, the bond is slashed and established standing is revoked. A sybil farm must therefore lock distinct capital and distinct hardware entropy for each head, so the cost of adding identities grows linearly instead of staying near zero.
